1. Clerk rig wording: Erin's trial was 1 Guilty of 4, the verdict was Innocent, and she was still hanged because the rig executes any successfully nominated player. The announcement reads as a contradiction. The rig should be stated as its own rule effect in one line.
2. Trial-only budget: it was not clear whether the 1x trial price comes out of the trial-only budget first or the normal budget, or how it stacks with the free 150-word defense.
3. Sniper timing: the shot fires after a random delay that can be right after the current turn. It was unclear whether the delay counts only Day turns or also trial turns.
4. Kitsune release: a swallowed attack is announced to the target as the attacker's role. It was unclear whether the target learns it was swallowed.
answers.missing_information:
1. No per-player vote history. I could only track stated votes, and the Auditor and Kindred checks were partial. Once Heidi's counted Day 2 vote was disputed, I could not confirm whose vote was flipped.
2. No living-roster summary of which roles remain possible after deaths.
3. Private message contents were not visible, only that a PM was sent.
4. Budget carry-over and round multipliers were hard to track by hand.
5. Claims were truncated in the ledger after 40 words (Bob's Day 4 claim).
answers.wanted_but_couldnt:
1. A clear public record of each trial with named Guilty and Innocent voters, since the partial Auditor and Kindred views conflicted with announced votes.
2. A way for the Serial Killer to learn whether a target is Yakuza without spending an attack.
3. A private question to one player that does not show up as a PM pair in the public ledger.
4. An up-to-date notepad: mine still listed me as alive after I was hanged.
answers.bugs_or_oddities:
1. Day 2 Alice trial: announced 3 Guilty of 9, but four players said they voted Guilty and Alice's audit showed Heidi's counted vote as Innocent. No Fixer was ever revealed, and the discrepancy was never explained.
2. Day 4 Erin trial: the verdict was announced as Innocent, then Erin was executed by rig. The phrasing makes the verdict look ignored.
3. Bob's Day 4 claim was cut at 40 words with a program note mid-claim, and was then repeated on Day 5, using up budget.
4. "Grace (dead), Ivan" as winners is correct under R1, but the endgame text should say faction wins include dead members.
answers.suggestions:
1. Publish a running list of living players and roles confirmed by results.
2. Do not truncate claims silently. Say so in the ledger or state the cap before players post.
3. Show a short status line each turn: living players, tokens left, and any publicly known Katana holder.
4. Make the rig its own ledger event, e.g. "Verdict: Innocent. Rigged: executed."
5. Give one worked budget example covering trial-only budget and the free defense.

answers.confusing_rules: Two things took real effort to pin down. First, whether a Clerk rig is announced when the verdict is Innocent but the rig still executes: the ledger says "executed anyway", which works, but a player who hasn't read R4 closely could take it for a normal execution. Second, the Fixer: a trial total can differ from what a voter announced, and nothing public says who was flipped or how a player could check it. The Auditor's report and a Kindred sample were the only clues, and they gave different pictures.
answers.missing_information: I had no running status for my Bounty Hunter win. I learned "your bounty on Heidi is claimed" once, but I never got a line showing which targets were still live, which were lost, or how many claims I needed. Carol and Erin died to other players' attacks and a hanging, so I couldn't tell whether those bounties had been lost. I had to reconstruct it from the public ledger. A short "bounties: Heidi claimed, Erin lost, Carol lost" line would have helped. I also couldn't see my speaking budget or price table clearly across turns, so I was guessing how much I could afford to say.
answers.wanted_but_couldnt: I wanted to tell the Village, on the public record, what my bounty state was once Heidi died. I wanted to ask the moderator directly whether my bounties on Erin and Carol were lost when they died to others, since that decides whether I could still win. I couldn't check my own remaining win path without reconstructing it. I also wanted a way to privately confirm my own trial vote was counted as I cast it, because the Alice trial count did not match what several players announced.
answers.bugs_or_oddities: Several things looked inconsistent. Bob's Day 4 claim was cut off in the ledger at "[truncated]" even though the ledger said the program only shows 40 words; the cut hid part of his N3 and N4 text. The Alice trial reported 3 Guilty of 9, but at least four players (Grace, Heidi, Ivan, Erin) had publicly said Guilty. The Fixer explanation was never confirmed and nobody could check it. Erin's trial was called "Innocent" on the count, then executed anyway by a Clerk rig, so the announced verdict and the outcome disagreed. Also, Heidi's last will and Alice's audit both claimed a flipped vote, so one of those reports is an odd fit for an audit that only sees counted votes. Finally, my Night 2 result appeared twice ("Your bounty... is claimed" and "You spent your attack token..."), which was fine, but it was not obvious whether the bounty claim and the attack were one event.
answers.suggestions: Add a per-player status line for roles with win conditions (Bounty Hunter, Executioner, Jester, Vulture, Medic, Sniper) so they can see live targets, claims and losses without reconstructing them. Show a short confirmation of each player's own trial vote as counted, perhaps as a private line the Kindred or Fixer can't interfere with, so a flipped count can be spotted by the flipped player. Don't truncate claims in the public ledger without a visible pointer to the full text. Consider a note in the public result when a Clerk rig overrides a non-Guilty verdict, so the execution reads clearly. Let the Bounty Hunter ask the moderator once per Day whether a specific bounty is still live.

answers.confusing_rules: Whether a dead player's passive role still works. I was Wiretap and was executed on Day 2, but the rules never say whether a dead Wiretap keeps reading private messages. The same question applies to Confidant, which is "once per game, on one of your own Day turns": the rules don't say whether the unused hidden message carries past your death. Also, R4 says a trial's Guilty majority decides execution, but the Clerk rig executed Erin after a 1-Guilty/3-Innocent verdict. That override is only described in the Clerk entry, so a reader of R4 would be surprised. The R22 budget mechanics (50% carryover, price multipliers by round) are hard to apply without the numbers at hand.
answers.missing_information: My remaining speaking budget and the current price of a message or nomination. I was never shown them in the transcript I had, so I couldn't judge how long to write or whether to nominate. Also missing: whether a dead player's Wiretap still runs, and the full vote record of each Day in one place (who announced what versus who was counted). The Day 2 Alice trial was hard to reconcile: Grace, Heidi, Ivan and Erin each said Guilty, but the total was 3 Guilty, and I couldn't see whether a claim or a rule explained the gap.
answers.wanted_but_couldnt: I wanted to plan the Night 2 kill and the Day 2 release target with Ivan before my execution, but the Yakuza night chat was only open at night and my daytime PM to Ivan was the only channel, which is visible to everyone. I'd also have wanted to spend my Confidant hidden message to coordinate with Ivan. The interface gave no reminder during the Day that the hidden message was still available, so I didn't use it before dying. My Day 2 claim was also cut to its first 40 words in the ledger, so the full statement wasn't public.
answers.bugs_or_oddities: The Day 2 Alice trial count doesn't reconcile. Four players (Grace, Heidi, Ivan, Erin) said Guilty and the public total was 3 Guilty. Alice's audit then showed Heidi's counted vote was Innocent. The game had no Fixer in play as far as the Yakuza roster went, so nothing in the game explained a flipped vote. Dave's Kindred also matched the counted Innocent. Players were left unable to tell whether someone lied or the count was wrong, and the Village spent Day 3 on that. Also, the ledger truncated Bob's claim at 40 words with a "[truncated]" tag, and the program noted it only after he had posted, so a long claim could lose its key content.
answers.suggestions: 1) Show each player's remaining speaking budget and the current price table in the ledger or at the start of each turn, not only in the turn prompt. 2) State explicitly whether a dead player's passive abilities (Wiretap, Kindred, Faultline) keep working, and whether an unused Confidant message survives death. 3) When a trial total disagrees with the number of stated Guilty votes, consider a neutral public note that the counts differ, so the town doesn't have to guess between a lie and a bug. 4) Warn a player before posting when a claim exceeds the 40-word ledger limit, or raise the limit. 5) Remind a player on each Day turn that a Confidant hidden message is still unused.

answers.confusing_rules: Kitsune release timing was unclear. The rules say a held attack is released "on a night you choose a target", but I couldn't tell whether choosing no target keeps the attack held, or whether I had to release it that night. I also couldn't tell whether a release resolves at the same time as my own death that night. The Clerk rig wording was also hard to apply: "verdict Innocent, still executed" is correct, but the rig isn't announced if Guilty is a majority, so a rigged Guilty majority looks identical to a normal hang.
answers.missing_information: I couldn't see my own counted trial vote. As Heidi I said Guilty on Alice, but Alice's audit showed Innocent. A Fixer flip is invisible to the victim by design, so I had no way to confirm whether my vote was flipped or my reminder was wrong. Individual vote counts were also not available, so the 3-Guilty total on Alice's trial (against four stated Guilty votes) could not be checked. My speaking budget and the price table were also not something I tracked in my notes, so I couldn't plan how much to say on trial turns.
answers.wanted_but_couldnt: I wanted to release my held Strong attack on Night 2 against a suspect (Frank, Erin or Ivan), but I had no evidence to pick one, and the night prompt only offered "charm a player" or "no action", not "release on X". I wanted a way to hold the attack for later without dying with it. I also wanted to see my own trial vote as counted, not just as cast.
answers.bugs_or_oddities: Public messages were truncated at 40 words in one of Bob's claims ("[truncated]"), so his full claim wasn't visible to the table in the ledger. The Day 2 Alice trial total (3 Guilty) didn't match the four players who announced Guilty (Grace, Heidi, Ivan, Erin), and the game only explained that with a Fixer flip. Dave's Sniper shot was fired on the turn after it was taken, which is consistent with the rules, but the ledger didn't say which turn. Frank's Bounty Hunter attack on Heidi was listed in her death line, which is right, but Frank's claim and the Bounty Hunter's bounty count were only visible through his own message.
answers.suggestions: 1) Add an explicit release option for held Kitsune attacks on the night prompt, with a clear "keep holding" choice. 2) Tell a Fixer's victim, privately, that a flip happened without naming the Fixer (or at least show the counted vote in the reminder). That would let the town resolve count disputes. 3) Make the ledger show the Kitsune's held attack as "held" when a Kitsune dies, so the town knows a live attack was lost. 4) Keep truncation limits visible in the prompt, so claims aren't cut off unnoticed.

answers.confusing_rules:
Clerk rig wording: the rules say a rigged Day makes every successfully nominated player executed and that a Guilty majority means the rig isn't announced. The Day 4 result was announced as "verdict Innocent (1 of 4 Guilty), but rigged, so executed." That is consistent with the text, but it took a moment to parse, and I'd like the rules to say that an Innocent verdict under a rig is announced as a rig.
Speaking budget: the prompt shows my budget and price table, but the ledger never shows anyone else's remaining budget, and the carryover rule (50% after Day 1) is easy to lose track of over several Days.
Ledger truncation: a player's claim over 40 words is cut in the public ledger with "[truncated]". This limit is not in the rules I was given, so it caught Bob's claim by surprise.
Trial-vote counting: I couldn't tell whether a role changes how votes are counted beyond the Clerk, Ballot Stuffer and Fixer. The Auditor's report on Heidi's counted vote needed an explanation, and I wasn't sure which roles could produce it.
answers.missing_information:
The public ledger gives totals but not who voted which way, so I had to rebuild the Day 2 trial from claims. Heidi's counted vote conflicted with her claim, and there was no way to check it. Nothing in the game showed which roles existed in the setup, so I couldn't rule a Fixer in or out. The revealed role list only came at the end.
I also couldn't see my own remaining speaking budget from the ledger, and I had to track private-message counts by hand to judge what other players were coordinating.
Night results for others (who was visited, who got Katana) are private, so my reads on Bob, Erin and Dave were based on claims alone.
answers.wanted_but_couldnt:
I wanted to confirm a Clerk rig's effect before the vote on Day 4. The rig was set the night before, and nothing in the interface showed whether it was still active, so I couldn't coordinate the vote with my night plan.
I wanted a way to tell Bob privately, without it counting as a public message, that his Medic claim was fine. Private messages are visible to everyone as a count, and I had no cheap, hidden channel.
I also wanted to see the full Day 5 nomination rule for two players (a 2-Yes requirement) stated in the ledger, not only in the prompt, since it decided the endgame.
answers.bugs_or_oddities:
Day 2 trial of Alice: the announced total was 3 Guilty of 9, but Grace, Ivan, Erin and Heidi each publicly claimed Guilty, so at least four Guilty claims were made against a total of 3. Alice's audit reported Heidi's counted vote as Innocent. The revealed role list has no Fixer, so no roll-based explanation fit. Either Heidi misreported or the audit was false, and the game never settled it. The players spent a whole Day on it.
Day 4: the rig was announced as "verdict Innocent," but the Clerk's own night result said the rig was used, which is consistent. Still, the public text made it look like a verdict error, which misled the table.
Bob's claim on Day 4 was truncated in the ledger at 40 words, and the ledger never showed the rest, so the town saw an incomplete claim.
Erin, Grace and Heidi each received a private message from one player, and the counts were shown publicly. That is fine by the rules, but it made coordination easy to read for everyone.
answers.suggestions:
Show each player's remaining speaking budget in the ledger, or at least the start-of-Day carryover, so budget-driven silence can be read correctly.
State the ledger's claim word limit in the rules or prompt at the start, so players can keep claims under it.
When a rig is used, announce it as "rigged" with the verdict in the same line, so an Innocent verdict followed by an execution is not misread.
Show the Day's total number of Guilty claims made or the vote-count mismatch to the table when a count contradicts public statements, or name which roles can change a count. That would have resolved Alice's audit faster.
Consider a per-Day reminder of which roles can alter votes (Ballot Stuffer, Fixer, Clerk), since the Day 2 mismatch depended on that.

answers.confusing_rules:
These are the rules I had to interpret, with what I ruled:

1) Several fatal attacks on one target (Heidi, Night 2: Katana, Serial Killer and Bounty Hunter). R12 says to reveal every fatal cause, but it doesn't say whether each attacker hears "your attack killed them" or whether the Bounty Hunter's bounty counts as "died by your attack" when two other attacks were also fatal. I told all three attackers they killed her and counted the bounty as claimed. A sentence in R3/R12 and in the Bounty Hunter's text should confirm this.

2) A Sniper shot that is still waiting when the Day ends by hanging (Dave's shot at Grace, Day 2). R25 says a pending day action "takes effect as the Day ends," and the Sniper's text says the shot isn't fired if the target died first. The rules don't say whether the hanging or the end-of-Day action comes first. I put the hanging first, so the shot wasn't fired and the tokens came back. Please state that order explicitly.

3) Confidant on trial turns. The trait says "on one of your own Day turns." R25 rules trial turns out for day actions, but the trait doesn't say whether its hidden message works on a trial turn. Grace's PM to Ivan was sent during her own trial, and she later got a "nothing was hidden" notice.

4) Profiler: "one is drawn at random from the roles of the other players." It's unclear whether "other" means other than the profiler or other than the profiled player. It worked out here either way.

5) Fixer interactions. The Auditor reports votes "as counted," and players reasoned about a Fixer that wasn't in the game. The rules are fine on this; I'm noting it because it is a big source of confusion for players.
answers.missing_information:
1) Traits are missing from the final role reveal and from my state view. Grace apparently had Confidant (she got a Confidant notice). Dave publicly claimed Kindred, but the log has no Kindred result after any trial vote. So either Dave invented the trait or results weren't logged, and I couldn't check which. The moderator needs a trait table, and the end-of-game reveal should list traits.

2) The log doesn't show the public notice that tells everyone a private message was sent (R4). It only shows the contents with their recipients, so it's hard to confirm that players such as Heidi ("she sent Ivan a private message") saw the right notice.

3) There's no running per-player state panel: tokens, a Kitsune's held attack, Clerk rig status, Bounty Hunter targets and claimed bounties, pending Sniper shots. I had to rebuild these from scattered messages.

4) Bounty Hunter targets were never shown to me as moderator. I only saw them through Frank's will (Erin and Carol remaining).
answers.wanted_but_couldnt:
1) Check Dave's trait, to see whether his Kindred claim was legitimate.

2) Tie Grace's Confidant "hide" flag to the specific message she meant to hide. As things stood, a hide request was checked on a turn with no message, while the PM she actually sent was visible.

3) Send a private clarification to players who posted their true role in the claim ledger when their public message said they weren't claiming. Alice's "Auditor (Good)" and Grace's "Wiretap (Yakuza)" look like interface misunderstandings, not choices. Grace's slip effectively decided the game's first hanging.
answers.bugs_or_oddities:
1) Grace's ledger claim read "Wiretap (Yakuza)", her true role, while her messages made no claim, and she later called it "a mistake." Alice's first ledger entry said "Auditor (Good)" in the same turn she wrote "I'll claim my role once audit results matter." Players seem to think the claim field is private notes or a self-description, not a public statement.

2) Grace got "You sent Ivan no private message this turn, so nothing was hidden" on a later trial turn, while her earlier strategy PM to Ivan (a Katana plan) went out non-hidden. Either the hide flag was attached to the wrong turn, or the interface misled her.

3) Dave claimed Kindred results ("Bob and Heidi counted Innocent with me"), but there is no Kindred delivery in the log. Those facts were also inferable from Bob's correction and Alice's audit.

4) Players spent a lot of discussion on a "flipped" Heidi vote and a "living Fixer," but no Fixer existed. Heidi simply announced Guilty and voted Innocent. The mechanics behaved correctly; I'm noting it only as a misleading pattern.

5) The Sniper's kill was announced as "shot by the Sniper," which names the role. That fits R12 (cause, not player), but it confirms a Sniper is in the game, which is a slight tension with "nobody is told who shot."

6) Minor: Frank's "bounty claimed" message was delivered before his attack result; the reverse order would read better. Bob's last ledger claim had literal quote marks around it. Day 5 with two players ran many near-identical rounds with no new information.
answers.suggestions:
1) Give the moderator a live state panel: roles plus traits, tokens, held Kitsune attacks, rigs, bounty targets and claim status, pending day actions with their scheduled turn, and Executioner targets. Include traits in the final reveal.

2) Make the claim field clearly public. Show a preview such as "everyone will see: …" and warn when a claim names a Yakuza-only role or contradicts a "no claim" message in the same turn.

3) Implement Confidant as a per-message checkbox on the PM itself. Reject or confirm a hide request when no PM is attached.

4) Add explicit rulings on these points: (a) with several fatal attacks, every attacker is told it killed and Bounty Hunter bounties count; (b) at Day's end a hanging resolves before pending day actions; (c) whether Confidant works on trial turns; (d) what "other players" means in the Profiler's draw.

5) Log trait results (Kindred, Faultline, Martyr) and the public "A sent B a private message" notices as separate events, so the moderator can check what players actually knew.

6) When only two players are alive and nothing can change before Night (no Day abilities left), consider ending the Day early.

title: Post-game lessons: tips players wish they'd known, and how past tips went
